full_text_en:
Weifu International Limited v. Huang Jianrong, Shanghai Haicheng Resources (Group) Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over service contract

Ruling Gist

The determination of joint and several liability must be based on clear legal provisions or contractual stipulations, and such liability cannot be arbitrarily imposed through the exercise of discretionary power.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial No. 91

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Huang Jianrong, male, born on October 3, 1957, Han ethnicity, residing at Jing'an District, Shanghai.

Agent ad litem: Qian Qian, attorney at Shanghai Hongqiao Zhenghan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xiao Yi, attorney at Shanghai Hongqiao Zhenghan Law Firm.

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shanghai Haicheng Resources (Group) Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 1201-08, No. 305 Liuying Road, Jing'an District, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Huang Jianrong, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Qian Qian, attorney at Shanghai Hongqiao Zhenghan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xiao Yi, attorney at Shanghai Hongqiao Zhenghan Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Weifu International Limited, domiciled at Unit B, 7/F, Kai Fat Building, No. 204-210 Wing Lok Street, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Legal Representative: Sheng Yongping, Director of the company.

Agent ad litem: Li Ciling, attorney at Shanghai Licheng Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Shanghai Panshi Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room H666, 6/F, Zone H (East Tower), No. 666 East Beijing Road, Huangpu District, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Wang Liqun, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Jin Chun, attorney at Beijing Huicheng Law Firm, Shanghai Branch.

The retrial applicants Huang Jianrong and Shanghai Haicheng Resources (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haicheng Company), in their dispute over a service contract with the respondent Weifu International Limited (hereinafter referred to as Weifu Company) and the third party at first instance Shanghai Panshi Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Panshi Company), applied to this Court for retrial, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2020) Hu Min Zhong No. 308 rendered by the Shanghai High People's Court. This Court, by civil ruling (2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 7091 dated December 13, 2021, ordered a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing in this case. The retrial applicants Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company's agents ad litem Qian Qian and Xiao Yi, the respondent Weifu Company's agent ad litem Li Ciling, and the third party at first instance Panshi Company's legal representative Wang Liqun and agent ad litem Jin Chun appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company applied for retrial with the following requests: 1. To set aside the civil judgment (2020) Hu Min Zhong No. 308 of the Shanghai High People's Court and the civil judgment (2018) Hu 02 Min Chu No. 1164 of the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, and to dismiss all of Weifu Company's claims; 2. To order Weifu Company to bear the case acceptance fees for the first and second instances. The main facts and reasons are as follows: (I) The original trial judgment erroneously determined that the condition for Huang Jianrong to pay service fees to Weifu Company had been satisfied. 1. The original trial judgment erroneously determined the scope of services provided by Weifu Company. According to Article 2 of the Consulting Intermediary Agreement involved in this case, the scope of Weifu Company's services should be "introducing investment and financing parties" and services related to recommending investment and financing parties, rather than "investment and financing." Throughout the entire transaction process, there was no investment or financing party introduced by Weifu Company, nor did Weifu Company perform any work related to introducing investment and financing parties, thus failing to fulfill the obligations stipulated in the Consulting Intermediary Agreement. The services related to "debt restructuring" are different from those related to "introducing investment and financing parties." Although Lu Jilin introduced Wang Liqun, the legal representative of Panshi Company, to Haicheng Company, Panshi Company is a service provider for the debt restructuring of Haicheng Company. Based on this, it cannot be concluded that Lu Jilin completed the obligations stipulated in the Consulting Intermediary Agreement. Moreover, during the debt restructuring phase, neither Weifu Company nor Lu Jilin provided any services. 2. The "services" were provided by Lu Jilin as an individual, not by Weifu Company, and there is no evidence to prove that Lu Jilin was an employee of Weifu Company. 3. At the time of signing the Consulting Intermediary Agreement, the relevant debt restructuring plan was already close to maturity. Huang Jianrong signed the Consulting Intermediary Agreement with Weifu Company not for payment purposes, but to help Lu Jilin reimburse personal expenses. The agreement itself was impossible to perform. 4. During the original trial, Weifu Company listed a series of so-called "various works" and submitted a cost expenditure list. However, the vast majority of this evidence is irrelevant to this case, and some facts were fabricated by Lu Jilin. (II) The original trial judgment erroneously ordered Haicheng Company to bear joint and several liability. Joint and several liability is a significant form of liability assumption, which should be formed by explicit legal provisions or clear stipulations by the parties, and cannot be arbitrarily determined through the court's discretionary power. In this case, the parties to the Consulting Intermediary Agreement involved were only Huang Jianrong and Weifu Company, and the agreement was signed by Huang Jianrong in his personal capacity, not on behalf of Haicheng Company. Therefore, the Consulting Intermediary Agreement is unrelated to Haicheng Company. There is no expression of intent to make Haicheng Company bear joint and several liability outside the agreement. In the absence of a contractual stipulation or legal provision, the original trial judgment erroneously ordered Haicheng Company to bear joint and several liability based on the principle of fairness.

Weifu Company argued in defense: (I) Weifu Company has fulfilled the obligations stipulated in the Consulting Intermediary Agreement and is entitled to receive service remuneration. 1. Investment and financing is a broad concept, and debt restructuring falls within the scope of investment and financing. During the service process of the project involved, Weifu Company invested substantial human resources, material resources, and energy. In the early stages, it carried out extensive work including promotion, visits, research, negotiations, coordination, and screening of plans, ultimately selecting the debt restructuring plan of Panshi Company. Later, when the China Securities Regulatory Commission (hereinafter referred to as CSRC) did not approve Haicheng Company's debt restructuring plan, Weifu Company used its extensive resources to coordinate and promote the implementation of the project. Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company have never denied the important role played by Weifu Company in the service process of the project involved. 2. At the end of November 2012, after the plan to resolve the massive debt of RMB 1.4 billion of Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company through debt restructuring was determined, Huang Jianrong, Haicheng Company, Weifu Company, and Panshi Company respectively signed the Consulting Intermediary Agreement and the Financial Advisory Agreement involved in this case, which can prove that Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company fully recognized Weifu Company's work. 3. Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company claim that the Consulting Intermediary Agreement was signed to reimburse Lu Jilin's expenses, which is inconsistent with the facts. Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company never raised this claim during the original trial. The statement by Wang Liqun, legal representative of Panshi Company, that "on November 26, 2012, Huang Jianrong and Lu Jilin were both in my office. Lu Jilin needed reimbursement, and Huang Jianrong helped sign an agreement with the Hong Kong (Weifu) company" contradicts Panshi Company's original trial statement that "we did not know there was an agreement between the plaintiff and Huang Jianrong" and constitutes a false statement. (II) Haicheng Company should bear joint and several liability in accordance with the law. 1. The preamble of the Consulting Intermediary Agreement states "regarding the investment and financing project of Party A's Tazhong Mining," and Huang Jianrong does not directly hold shares in Tazhong Mining. Therefore, Party A under the agreement should refer to Haicheng Company. 2. As the legal representative and actual controller of Haicheng Company, Huang Jianrong holds 20% of the equity in Haicheng Company. Based on apparent authority, Weifu Company believed that Huang Jianrong had the right to directly sign agreements on behalf of Haicheng Company externally. 3. Circumstances such as Haicheng Company's Vice President Zhang Jieyuan actively communicating with Weifu Company on behalf of Haicheng Company, and Haicheng Company accepting services from Weifu Company, indicate that Haicheng Company was the actual contracting party to the Consulting Intermediary Agreement. The defect in the absence of Haicheng Company's seal on the agreement has been remedied through actual performance. 4. As the actual beneficiary of the Consulting Intermediary Agreement, Haicheng Company should bear the corresponding legal obligations. Otherwise, it would lead to an imbalance of rights and obligations, violating the principle of good faith.

Panshi Company stated: The debt restructuring of the project involved was primarily handled by Panshi Company. Weifu Company and Lu Jilin did not participate in it. Weifu Company and Lu Jilin never attended debt restructuring meetings, nor did they provide any direct evidence proving that they provided services for the debt restructuring. The contents regarding Panshi Company and its legal representative Wang Liqun in the "Preliminary Statistical Table of Direct Costs Borne by Weifu Company for Providing Investment and Financing Consulting Services for the Tazhong Mining Debt-to-Equity Swap Project (Including Panshi Company) of Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company" submitted by Weifu Company after the first instance trial are not true.

Claims of Weifu Company at first instance: 1. To order Huang Jianrong to pay Weifu Company consulting intermediary service fees of RMB 28,989,871.02; 2. To order Haicheng Company to bear joint and several liability for the payment of the above fees to Weifu Company; 3. The litigation costs of this case to be borne jointly by Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company.

Facts found by the court of first instance: Huang Jianrong and Huang Ying are shareholders of Haicheng Company; Haicheng Company is a shareholder of Xinjiang Tacheng International Resources Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinjiang Tacheng Company); Xinjiang Tacheng Company holds equity in Tazhong Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tazhong Mining Company) and is a shareholder of Tibet Zhufeng Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tibet Zhufeng Company) and China Global New Technology Import and Export Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhonghuanji Company); Huang Jianrong is the legal representative of Haicheng Company, Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Tibet Zhufeng Company, and Zhonghuanji Company. Lu Jilin is an employee of Weifu Company.

On October 14, 2011, a third party, Dongfang International Group Shanghai Foreign Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongfang Foreign Trade Company), filed a lawsuit against Haicheng Company, Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Huang Jianrong, Huang Ying, Zhonghuanji Company, Tazhong Mining Company, and Zhonghuanji (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in the Shanghai High People's Court, requesting that Haicheng Company pay RMB 1,205,062,762.39 for goods, agency fees, and damages for delayed performance, that Dongfang Foreign Trade Company be entitled to dispose of 92% of the equity in Tazhong Mining Company held by Xinjiang Tacheng Company and have priority in repayment within RMB 1.2 billion, and that Huang Jianrong, Huang Ying, Zhonghuanji (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Zhonghuanji Company, and Tazhong Mining Company bear joint and several compensation liability within a certain scope. The Shanghai High People's Court, based on the application of Dongfang Foreign Trade Company, issued a civil ruling and took property preservation measures against the defendants in the case.

In early 2012, Huang Jianrong approached Liu Jianwei, the former General Manager of Dongfang Foreign Trade Company, to discuss resolving the above debt issues. Liu Jianwei introduced Lu Jilin to Huang Jianrong.

On July 31, 2012, Weifu Company and Shanghai Donghao International Business Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Donghao Company) signed a "Cooperation Agreement," stipulating: Whereas Haicheng Company, with Huang Jianrong as its actual controller, was in a debt crisis due to the civil lawsuit and related preservation measures initiated by Dongfang Foreign Trade Company, and in order to resolve the massive debt, Weifu Company had reached an oral agreement with Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company on the consulting intermediary work for introducing strategic investors to Tazhong Mining Company. Weifu Company agreed to provide consulting intermediary services for the investment and financing project to Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company. Therefore, Weifu Company intended to cooperate with Donghao Company on the consulting intermediary project, with Donghao Company acting as an assistant in the project, fully participating in the consulting intermediary work provided by Weifu Company to Huang Jianrong, etc. The rights and obligations of Donghao Company mainly included organizing and preparing meetings related to the project, arranging meeting schedules and venues, conducting business investigation work related to the project, and performing liaison work related to the project and signing the consulting intermediary agreement.

In August 2012, Li Jing, an employee of Donghao Company, arranged investment invitation negotiations, with the participation of relevant personnel from Weifu Company (Lu Jilin), Xinxing Cathay International Group, Pengxin Group, Guo's Group, Gaodeng Group, Greenland Group, and Panshi Company. Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company discussed and screened the financing plans of the various parties.

On August 10, 2012, Sun Hua, Secretary of the Board of Directors of Tibet Zhufeng Company, sent two emails to Lu Jilin and Li Jing, with the subjects "Cooperation Plan for Introducing Strategic Investors to Tazhong Mining Company" and "Report on Kyrgyzstan Mining Project." On October 10, Sun Hua sent two emails to Lu Jilin and Li Jing, stating "Dear General Lu, as requested by the Chairman, I am sending the following materials to you," with the subjects "Analysis and Explanation of the Tibet Zhufeng Restructuring Plan (I)" and "Analysis and Explanation of the Tibet Zhufeng Restructuring Plan (II)," and attachments "Analysis and Explanation of the Tibet Zhufeng Restructuring Plan," "Summary of Non-Public Issuance of Stock Plan," and "Summary of Major Asset Restructuring Plan." On November 20, Li Jing sent an email to Sun Hua stating, "After discussion between Chairman Huang and General Lu, the following inspection team members will go to Tazhong Mining Company in Tajikistan for on-site inspection around December 10-15: Lu Jilin, WEI GORDON MINQUAN, Li Jing. Attached are scanned copies of their passports. Please assist with visa invitation matters for Tajikistan." Subsequently, Sun Hua replied, "Received. I will arrange." On November 21, Zhang Jieyuan of Haicheng Company sent an email to Li Jing with an attachment titled "Mediation Agreement (Revised Version 11.19)."

On November 26, 2012, Huang Jianrong (Party A) and Weifu Company (Party B) signed the "Consulting Intermediary Agreement," stipulating: The parties have, through friendly consultations regarding Party A's Tazhong Mining Company equity investment and financing project, agreed that Party A entrusts Party B with the consulting intermediary work for the project. Party A's rights and obligations include providing relevant materials for the project, having the final decision-making power over the project during negotiations, and paying Party B's fees on time in accordance with the agreement. Party B's rights and obligations include recommending investment and financing parties for the project, receiving and organizing on-site inspections by investment and financing parties, communicating with investment and financing parties, and collecting fees in accordance with the agreement. The consulting intermediary fee is 2% of the investment and financing amount, and within five working days after the completion of the investment and financing (taking the date of funds in place as the standard), Party A shall complete the payment to Party B. All taxes and fees related to this contract shall be borne by the parties respectively.

In November 2012, Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Panshi Company, Haicheng Company, and Huang Jianrong signed a "Financial Advisory Framework Agreement" and a "Supplementary Financial Advisory Agreement." The main content of the "Financial Advisory Framework Agreement" was: Xinjiang Tacheng Company entrusts Panshi Company, under the terms and conditions stipulated in this agreement, as the financial advisor for the debt restructuring plan for which the confirmed debt amount is RMB 1.2 billion among Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Haicheng Company, Huang Jianrong, and Dongfang Foreign Trade Company, to provide services under this agreement for this debt restructuring. After the completion of the debt restructuring by Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Panshi Company shall serve as the long-term exclusive financial advisor for Xinjiang Tacheng Company. If Xinjiang Tacheng Company engages any third party to complete any future round of work covered by this agreement that falls within the scope of Panshi Company's work, Xinjiang Tacheng Company shall still pay the full corresponding advisory fees to Panshi Company in the manner agreed in this agreement. The financial advisory fee for the debt restructuring provided by Panshi Company to Xinjiang Tacheng Company is RMB 800,000, plus travel and accommodation expenses incurred for the financial advisory services. The "Supplementary Financial Advisory Agreement" stipulated: The parties agree that after Xinjiang Tacheng Company's IPO listing or the backdoor listing of Xinjiang Tacheng Company's main assets, and 10 days before the expiration of the lock-up period for the shares of the listed company held directly or indirectly by Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Panshi Company shall refund the RMB 800,000 financial advisory fee it has already collected from Xinjiang Tacheng Company. Within 15 days after the refund, Xinjiang Tacheng Company or a third party designated by it shall pay Panshi Company 1% of the shares corresponding to the assets injected into the IPO listed company or the backdoor listing. The method of payment for the above 1% shares may be negotiated separately at that time, but in any event, Panshi Company shall pay no further consideration for the shares it obtains.

On December 13, 2012, Dongfang Foreign Trade Company, Haicheng Company, Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Huang Jianrong, Huang Ying, Zhonghuanji Company, and Tazhong Mining Company jointly signed a "Mediation Agreement" numbered SHWMHC20121213, stipulating: The parties jointly confirm that as of June 30, 2012, the principal debt owed by Haicheng Company to Dongfang Foreign Trade Company is RMB 1.2 billion, with interest of RMB 200 million. After June 30, 2012, the principal for interest calculation shall be RMB 1.4 billion, with interest calculated at the bank loan interest rate for the same period until the actual date of repayment. Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Huang Jianrong, and Huang Ying jointly bear joint and several liability for the above debt. Huang Jianrong and Huang Ying provide their owned real estate as mortgage collateral. The method of repayment is: After the court issues a mediation letter based on the mediation agreement, and within two working days after the mediation letter takes effect, Xinjiang Tacheng Company shall transfer to Dongfang Foreign Trade Company 46.35 million shares (including fruits) of Western Mining Co., Ltd. held by it that have been pledged to Dongfang Foreign Trade Company, calculated at the weighted average price of the twenty trading days prior to the actual transfer date, deducting the taxes and fees required for the transfer, to offset the debt. The remaining debt shall be partially offset by Dongfang Foreign Trade Company through receiving part of the equity in Tazhong Mining Company held by Xinjiang Tacheng Company. After the debt offset, the parties agree to inject the entire equity of Tazhong Mining Company into Tibet Zhufeng Company for asset restructuring and final settlement. The specific handling method for the equity part of Tazhong Mining Company is: evaluation, audit, and due diligence of Tazhong Mining Company shall be completed; within 30 days after the completion of evaluation, audit, and due diligence, Xinjiang Tacheng Company shall transfer to Dongfang Foreign Trade Company 46% of the debt-offsetting equity it holds in Tazhong Mining Company, transferred at 46% of the registered capital ($30 million), i.e., $13.8 million (converted at an exchange rate of 6.24, equivalent to RMB 86.112 million). This amount shall be deducted from the interest-bearing principal on the same day the equity change registration is completed. After the completion of the equity transfer, the parties agree to inject the entire equity of Tazhong Mining Company into Tibet Zhufeng Company to achieve the asset restructuring of Tibet Zhufeng Company. If before June 1, 2014, the restructuring plan has been approved by the CSRC and Dongfang Foreign Trade Company has actually obtained shares of Tibet Zhufeng Company corresponding to 46% of Tazhong Mining Company's equity through the restructuring of Tibet Zhufeng Company, after the expiration of the lock-up period, Dongfang Foreign Trade Company has the right to sell the shares of Tibet Zhufeng Company it holds at a price it deems appropriate. If the proceeds from the sale, after deducting $13.8 million (equivalent to RMB 86.112 million) and all taxes and fees incurred by Dongfang Foreign Trade Company due to the receipt and transfer of Tazhong Mining Company equity, exceed the remaining portion, Dongfang Foreign Trade Company shall return the excess assets to Xinjiang Tacheng Company in the same form. On January 22, 2013, the above parties also signed a "Supplementary Agreement to the Mediation Agreement," further clarifying and supplementing the "Mediation Agreement."

On January 25, 2013, the Shanghai High People's Court, based on the above "Mediation Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement to the Mediation Agreement," issued a civil mediation letter (2011) Hu Gao Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi No. S5, the content of which is generally consistent with the "Mediation Agreement," and also stipulates the circumstances under which Dongfang Foreign Trade Company may apply to the court for enforcement.

On May 6, 2013, Zhang Jieyuan of Haicheng Company sent three emails to Li Jing, with attachments of "Explanation on Major Asset Restructuring of Xizang Zhufeng," "Civil Mediation Agreement," "Mediation Agreement and Supplementary Agreement to Mediation Agreement." On May 14, 2013, Zhang Jieyuan of Haicheng Company forwarded to Li Jing an email sent by Huang Jingyan of the Investment Department of Panshi Company to Zhang Jieyuan, with attachments of "Financial Advisory Agreement (Annual)" and "Supplementary Agreement to Financial Advisory Agreement (New)." On August 2, 2013, Li Jing sent the involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement via email to Huang Jingyan of Panshi Company.

On August 27, 2015, Xizang Zhufeng Company issued the "Announcement on the Results of the Company's Non-public Issuance of Shares and Changes in Share Capital," which disclosed: Xizang Zhufeng Company purchased the 100% equity of Tazhong Mining Company held collectively by Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Dongfang Waimao Company, and Zhonghuanji Company by means of issuing shares. The total number of shares issued by Xizang Zhufeng Company in this issuance was 494,673,930 shares, with each share priced at RMB 6.73. Among them, a total of 227,550,008 shares were issued to Dongfang Waimao Company, amounting to RMB 1,449,493,550.96.

In September 2015, Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Panshi Company, Haicheng Company, and Huang Jianrong signed the "Financial Advisory Supplementary Agreement II," stipulating: In accordance with the framework agreement and supplementary agreements, the advisory fee to be paid by Xinjiang Tacheng Company to Panshi Company shall be 4,946,739 shares of Xizang Zhufeng Company. From the date of signing this agreement, the ownership of the shares shall be transferred to Panshi Company, and the corresponding transfer procedures shall be handled in accordance with the law.

On October 29 and November 16, 2015, Lu Jilin of Weifu Company had two conversations with Huang Jianrong. The records of the conversations mainly reflect that Lu Jilin of Weifu Company inquired with Huang Jianrong regarding the agreements and proportions among Panshi Company, Weifu Company, and Haicheng Company concerning the collection of consulting fees. Huang Jianrong's main opinion was that Weifu Company's fees would be obtained from the fees paid by Panshi Company from the Haicheng Company side, with the proportion not less than 30%, but ultimately no tripartite agreement was reached. Thereafter, Weifu Company also sent text messages to Huang Jianrong multiple times regarding the fee collection matters.

On March 23, 2016, Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Panshi Company, Haicheng Company, and Huang Jianrong signed the "Financial Advisory Supplementary Agreement III," stipulating: The parties confirm that the financial advisory fee to be paid by Xinjiang Tacheng Company to Panshi Company shall be 4,946,739 shares of Xizang Zhufeng Company; within five days from the date of signing this agreement, Xinjiang Tacheng Company shall pay RMB 20 million to Panshi Company, and upon completion of such payment, Xinjiang Tacheng Company shall be deemed to have completed the payment of 2.5 million shares to Panshi Company; Panshi Company shall, through its affiliated company, continue to provide financial advisory consulting services to Xinjiang Tacheng Company with respect to the sums stipulated in this agreement, and the relevant parties will sign separate agreements; Haicheng Company and Huang Jianrong, as the actual controllers of Xizang Zhufeng Company, shall assume joint and several liability for the payment obligations of Xinjiang Tacheng Company stipulated in this agreement.

On June 24, 2016, Dongfang Waimao Company applied to the Shanghai High People's Court for enforcement. On July 7 of the same year, according to the Enforcement Ruling of the Shanghai High People's Court, the transfer procedures for the 227,550,008 restricted tradable shares of Xizang Zhufeng Company held by Dongfang Waimao Company were completed, and the claims under the aforementioned Civil Mediation Agreement were satisfied.

On July 12, 2016, Xizang Zhufeng Company issued the "Announcement in Response to the Inquiry Letter from the Shanghai Stock Exchange," which provided supplementary explanations on "the occurrence of the debt dispute with Dongfang Waimao Company, Dongfang Waimao Company becoming a shareholder of Tazhong Mining Company, Dongfang Waimao Company becoming a shareholder of Xizang Zhufeng Company, and the enforcement ruling process of this debt repayment." Among them, the part concerning "the enforcement ruling process of this debt repayment" stated: After the court accepted the application of Dongfang Waimao Company, Xinjiang Tacheng Company, as the person subject to enforcement, proposed a debt repayment plan involving the introduction of a third party. In accordance with Article 2, Paragraph 2 of the Mediation Agreement, the person subject to enforcement requested the third parties, Jiuzhou Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiuzhou Securities), Shanghai Geshi Xiangjin Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as Geshi Xiangjin), and natural person Liu Meibao, to repay the debts on its behalf according to the distribution plan. The above-mentioned third parties were to directly pay cash, including principal and interest, to Dongfang Waimao Company according to the distribution plan. Dongfang Waimao Company would deliver 215,330,000 of the 227,550,008 restricted shares of Xizang Zhufeng Company it held to the third parties according to the distribution plan, and the remaining 12,220,008 shares would be returned by Dongfang Waimao Company to Xinjiang Tacheng Company. All third parties sent letters to the court, expressly agreeing to repay the debts on behalf of the person subject to enforcement to Dongfang Waimao Company, accepting the debt repayment plan proposed by the person subject to enforcement, and Dongfang Waimao Company accepted this. Accordingly, the Shanghai High People's Court issued the Enforcement Ruling (2016) Hu Zhi No. 9: The third parties, Jiuzhou Securities, Geshi Xiangjin, and Liu Meibao, shall pay to Dongfang Waimao Company RMB 512.68 million, RMB 615.3 million, and RMB 172.3 million respectively; Dongfang Waimao Company shall return the 227,550,008 restricted shares of "Xizang Zhufeng" (stock code 600338) held by it to the person subject to enforcement. Among them, 83.33 million shares belong to third party Jiuzhou Securities, 100 million shares belong to third party Geshi Xiangjin, 32 million shares belong to third party Liu Meibao, and 12,220,008 shares are returned to Xinjiang Tacheng Company. As of July 7, 2016, the above-mentioned debt repayment funds have been paid, and the corresponding restricted tradable shares have also been transferred to the securities accounts of the respective relevant persons.

During the first instance trial, Weifu Company provided a copy of a Customer Satisfaction Survey Form, on which it stated: Company Name: "Panshi Company"; Client Name: "Haicheng Company, Chairman Huang Jianrong"; Project Name: "Debt restructuring between Haicheng Company and its legal representative and Dongfang Waimao, various related legal, financial, and tax consultations, consultation and communication with the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC) policies, project financing, merger and acquisition, etc., as exclusive financial advisor"; Project Source: "Introduced by Weifu Company"; Customer Satisfaction: "Very Satisfied"; Haicheng Company affixed its seal on the form.

The court of first instance rendered judgment: 1. Huang Jianrong shall pay service fee of RMB 28,989,871.02 to Weifu Company within ten days from the effective date of the judgment; 2. Haicheng Company shall bear joint and several liability for the payment obligation of Huang Jianrong in item 1 above. The case acceptance fee of RMB 186,749.36 shall be borne jointly by Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company.

Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, filed an appeal. The appellate requests of Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company were: to reverse the judgment of first instance, remand the case for retrial, or otherwise amend the judgment to dismiss all of Weifu Company's claims.

The court of second instance confirmed the facts found by the court of first instance.

During the second instance trial, Weifu Company submitted a written document to the court of second instance, stating that in order to quickly settle the dispute, it was willing to voluntarily reduce its claim from the first instance, and only requested that Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company pay service fee of RMB 14.9 million.

The court of second instance held: Regarding the application of law in this case, Weifu Company is a corporate legal person established in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and this case is a Hong Kong-related case. Since the performance of the involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement took place in Mainland China, and all parties in the first instance of this case unanimously chose to apply the law of Mainland China of the People's Republic of China, the law of Mainland China of the People's Republic of China shall apply to this case.

The issues in dispute in the second instance were: 1. The legal validity of the Consulting Intermediary Agreement; 2. Whether Weifu Company is entitled to claim service remuneration; 3. Whether Haicheng Company shall bear joint and several payment liability.

First, regarding the legal validity of the Consulting Intermediary Agreement. The involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement is a true expression of the parties' intent, and is lawful and valid. Although Weifu Company is a Hong Kong company, the investment and financing intermediation introduction and consulting matters involved in this case are not within the scope of prohibited or restricted market access. Therefore, the failure to register for business in Mainland China is not sufficient to render the Consulting Intermediary Agreement invalid.

Second, regarding the issue of whether Weifu Company is entitled to claim service remuneration. The core dispute among the parties is whether the "equity investment and financing project of Tazhong Mining Company" as stipulated in the Consulting Intermediary Agreement includes asset restructuring methods or only refers to the introduction of external funds. The court of second instance held that the stipulation on "investment and financing project" in the Consulting Intermediary Agreement is not clear and should be comprehensively determined by considering the background of signing the agreement, the circumstances of performance, and other aspects. First, from the background of signing the Consulting Intermediary Agreement, because Huang Jianrong, Haicheng Company, and other affiliated companies fell into a huge debt crisis, Huang Jianrong, in order to resolve the debt dispute, entrusted Weifu Company to carry out relevant financing consulting services. Therefore, the purpose of signing the Consulting Intermediary Agreement was to resolve the debt dispute, and there was no limitation on the means to resolve the debt crisis. Investment and financing include various methods. Huang Jianrong's claim that the investment and financing project stipulated in the Consulting Intermediary Agreement only refers to the introduction of external funds, excluding internal asset restructuring methods, lacks effective evidence to support it. Second, from the perspective of performance, before the signing of the Consulting Intermediary Agreement, Weifu Company had already entrusted Donghao Company to carry out a series of investment attraction and negotiation work. During this process, Weifu Company recommended Wang Liqun, the chairman of Panshi Company, to Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company. Combined with the emails exchanged between the parties, Haicheng Company sent to Li Jing of Donghao Company the relevant asset restructuring plan, mediation agreement, and the financial advisory agreement signed with Panshi Company. Although Weifu Company and Donghao Company did not directly participate in drafting the restructuring plan, Weifu Company's service work played an important role in promoting the restructuring plan and resolving the debt crisis. Third, from the recordings of subsequent negotiations among the parties, Huang Jianrong never denied that Weifu Company could obtain remuneration on the grounds that Weifu Company did not complete the introduction of external funds. Moreover, Huang Jianrong also indicated that the remuneration collected by Weifu Company should not be less than 30% of the remuneration obtained by Panshi Company. Although Huang Jianrong believed that the above remuneration should be paid by Panshi Company, there was no clear agreement among the parties on this. Based on the fact that Weifu Company carried out the involved financing consulting services at the entrustment of Huang Jianrong, and Huang Jianrong ultimately resolved the debt crisis as a result, Weifu Company is entitled to demand that Huang Jianrong pay corresponding service remuneration in accordance with the Consulting Intermediary Agreement. During the second instance trial, Weifu Company voluntarily adjusted its claim, only requesting that Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company pay RMB 14.9 million in service fees. Considering Weifu Company's performance and its contribution to the resolution of the entire debt dispute, the above remuneration amount is reasonable, and the court of second instance supported it.

Third, regarding whether Haicheng Company shall bear joint and several payment liability. Although Haicheng Company is not a signatory to the Consulting Intermediary Agreement, it is the principal debtor in the debt dispute case related to Dongfang Waimao Company and is the actual beneficiary of the asset restructuring plan involved in the case. Huang Jianrong, as the legal representative of Haicheng Company, entrusted Weifu Company to provide the involved financing services, which was actually an act carried out for the benefit of Haicheng Company. Therefore, Weifu Company's request that Haicheng Company bear joint and several liability for Huang Jianrong's payment obligation in this case should be supported.

The court of second instance rendered judgment: 1. Affirm item 2 of the Civil Judgment (2018) Hu 02 Min Chu No. 1164 of the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court; 2. Amend item 1 of the said judgment to: Huang Jianrong shall pay service fee of RMB 14.9 million to Weifu Company within ten days from the effective date of the judgment. The case acceptance fee for the first instance of RMB 186,749.36 shall be borne jointly by Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company in the amount of RMB 93,374.68, and by Weifu Company in the amount of RMB 93,374.68; the case acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 186,749.36 shall be borne jointly by Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company in the amount of RMB 93,374.68, and by Weifu Company in the amount of RMB 93,374.68.

During the retrial proceedings, the parties submitted new evidence regarding the retrial requests, and this court organized the parties to conduct cross-examination in accordance with the law.

Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company newly submitted three sets of evidence. The first set: An "Explanation of Facts Regarding the Case of Weifu Company and Huang Jianrong" issued by Wang Liqun. The purpose of proof is: Only if Lu Jilin found a suitable investor to take over the debt would Huang Jianrong pay a 2% commission; during the debt restructuring process, Lu Jilin did not provide any services; the signing of the involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement between Huang Jianrong and Lu Jilin was for reimbursement purposes; the expense vouchers previously submitted by Weifu Company are unrelated to this project. The second set: Testimony of witness Hua Wei, and a copy of an invoice from Jin Fayuan Restaurant. The purpose of proof is: The expense voucher table provided by Weifu Company to the original trial court contained false information; Hua Wei never received red wine on behalf of Huang Jianrong; on August 12, 2012, the expenses for the dinner meeting at Shanghai Jinyuan Club were borne by Huang Jianrong's side. The third set: Printed copies of 6 text messages exchanged between Tang Yun and Huang Jianrong and Wang Liqun. The purpose of proof is: The amount claimed by Lu Jilin was a commission fee obtained based on commercial practices after introducing Wang Liqun to provide services, not the 2% remuneration stipulated in the Consulting Intermediary Agreement; he never claimed the agreement remuneration from Huang Jianrong, but always claimed it from Wang Liqun.

Weifu Company's cross-examination opinions were: It does not recognize the authenticity and legality of the "Explanation of Facts Regarding the Case of Weifu Company and Huang Jianrong" issued by Wang Liqun, arguing that Wang Liqun, as the legal representative of the third party Panshi Company, cannot serve as a witness in accordance with the law; it recognizes the authenticity of witness Hua Wei's testimony, but does not recognize its relevance and legality, arguing that witness Hua Wei is a department manager of Xizang Zhufeng Company and has an interest in Huang Jianrong, and his testimony is not related to this case; it does not recognize the authenticity, relevance, and legality of the Jin Fayuan Restaurant invoice, as the invoice is not an original and its content is unrelated to this case; it does not recognize the authenticity of the printed copies of text messages exchanged between Tang Yun and Huang Jianrong and Wang Liqun, arguing that the content of the messages is incomplete and not notarized.

Panshi Company did not express cross-examination opinions.

Given that Weifu Company has no objection to the authenticity of witness Hua Wei's testimony submitted by Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company, this court confirms the authenticity of this evidence. The probative force of this evidence shall be determined in combination with the case facts and other evidence. Wang Liqun, as the legal representative of the first-instance third party Panshi Company, participated in the retrial trial, was examined on relevant issues, and made statements. Therefore, this court does not accept the "Explanation of Facts Regarding the Case of Weifu Company and Huang Jianrong" issued by Wang Liqun submitted by Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company. As for the copy of the Jin Fayuan Restaurant invoice and the printed copies of text messages exchanged between Tang Yun and Huang Jianrong and Wang Liqun submitted by Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company, because they are not originals and Weifu Company does not recognize their authenticity, this court also does not accept them.

This court confirms the facts found in the original trial, except for "Lu Jilin is an employee of Weifu Company."

This court holds: This case is a civil dispute arising from legal facts that occurred before the implementation of the Civil Code. Pursuant to Article 1, Paragraph 2 of the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Temporal Effect of the Application of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China," the provisions of the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time shall apply. According to Article 403 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," when a people's court hears a retrial case, it shall focus on the retrial requests. Based on the opinions of the parties in their pleadings, the issues in dispute in this retrial are: 1. Whether the original trial judgment ordering Huang Jianrong to pay service remuneration to Weifu Company is appropriate; 2. Whether the original trial judgment ordering Haicheng Company to bear joint and several liability for Huang Jianrong's obligation to pay service remuneration to Weifu Company is appropriate.

(1) Regarding the issue of whether the original trial judgment ordering Huang Jianrong to pay service remuneration to Weifu Company is appropriate. In this case, before signing the involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement, Weifu Company had already entrusted Donghao Company to carry out a series of investment attraction and negotiation work, and recommended Wang Liqun, the chairman of Panshi Company, to Huang Jianrong. On November 26, 2012, Huang Jianrong and Weifu Company signed the involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement, stipulating the payment standards and payment time for consulting intermediary fees. Meanwhile, Panshi Company, Xinjiang Tacheng Company, Haicheng Company, and Huang Jianrong signed the "Financial Advisory Framework Agreement" and supplementary agreements in November 2012. Thereafter, on December 13, 2012, Dongfang Waimao Company, Haicheng Company, Huang Jianrong, Tazhong Mining Company, and others signed the "Mediation Agreement" to resolve Haicheng Company's huge debt of RMB 1.4 billion through asset restructuring. The original trial court accordingly held that an asset restructuring plan of such scale and complexity should have been nearly completed by November 26, 2012. If the restructuring plan was unrelated to the "investment and financing" services provided by Weifu Company, then it would obviously be inconsistent with commercial logic for Huang Jianrong to sign the involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement with Weifu Company at that time, and this conclusion was not improper. Huang Jianrong, as a rational businessman, should have foreseen the consequences of signing the involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement. Analyzing the timing of his signing the agreement with Weifu Company, it can be inferred that Huang Jianrong recognized Weifu Company's work and was willing to pay corresponding intermediary service fees. The content of the two conversations between Lu Jilin and Huang Jianrong on October 29 and November 16, 2015, also confirms this. In summary, the original trial judgment, after comprehensively considering that Weifu Company had already provided certain intermediary services and that Huang Jianrong was willing to sign the involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement with Weifu Company when the asset restructuring plan was nearly completed, found that Weifu Company is entitled to demand that Huang Jianrong pay the corresponding service remuneration of RMB 14.9 million in accordance with the involved Consulting Intermediary Agreement, which is not improper.

Huang Jianrong argued that the "investment and financing" services stipulated in the Consulting Intermediary Agreement only referred to "introducing investors and financiers" and did not include internal asset restructuring. However, in light of the background to the execution of the Consulting Intermediary Agreement, the purpose of Huang Jianrong's signing of the Consulting Intermediary Agreement with Weifu Company was to resolve his own and the affiliated companies' (including Haicheng Company) substantial debt disputes, whereas the "investment and financing" services stipulated in the Consulting Intermediary Agreement themselves encompassed multiple methods. Under the circumstance that Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company had separately entered into agreements such as the Financial Advisory Framework Agreement and the Supplementary Financial Advisory Agreement with Panshi Company, in order to avoid overlap or conflict between the services of Weifu Company and Panshi Company, Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company should have clearly delineated the service content of the two companies in the relevant agreements. However, there is no evidence in this case to prove that this was done. Huang Jianrong argued that the debt restructuring was primarily led by Panshi Company, and that Weifu Company and Lu Jilin did not participate in any debt restructuring meetings or provide any written financing plans. Nevertheless, according to the Consulting Intermediary Agreement, "participating in debt restructuring meetings and formulating financing plans" was not an obligation that Weifu Company was required to perform, and their lack of participation in these specific actions cannot negate the work done by Weifu Company in the early stages of the restructuring. Huang Jianrong argued that Lu Jilin was not an employee of Weifu Company, but Huang Jianrong voluntarily signed the Consulting Intermediary Agreement with Weifu Company on the basis of the preliminary services provided by Lu Jilin. This is sufficient to prove that Huang Jianrong accepted that Weifu Company would succeed to the preliminary services provided by Lu Jilin. Therefore, whether Lu Jilin was an employee of Weifu Company does not affect Weifu Company's right to claim payment from Huang Jianrong under the Consulting Intermediary Agreement. Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company asserted that the purpose of signing the Consulting Intermediary Agreement was merely to help Lu Jilin reimburse personal expenses. However, this assertion was not raised in the first or second instance, and there is no corresponding evidence to support it. Accordingly, this court does not accept it. The testimony of witness Hua Wei, the dining expense invoices, and the relevant text message records submitted by Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company are insufficient to overturn the facts found by the original trial. In summary, Huang Jianrong's contention that the original trial judgment erroneously found that the condition for Huang Jianrong to pay the service fee to Weifu Company had been fulfilled cannot be sustained.

(2) Regarding the issue of whether it was appropriate for the original trial judgment to order Haicheng Company to assume joint and several liability for Huang Jianrong's obligation to pay service remuneration to Weifu Company. Joint and several liability is a statutory liability, arising from legal provisions or the agreement of the parties. Because joint and several liability imposes a relatively strict shared responsibility on the liable persons, placing them in a relatively disadvantageous position, the application of joint and several liability should follow the strict principle of legality. That is, a multi-party liability relationship cannot be arbitrarily identified as joint and several liability through the exercise of discretionary power; rather, joint and several liability can only be applied if there is a clear legal provision or contractual agreement. In this case, first, there is no clear legal basis for the original trial judgment to order Haicheng Company to assume joint and several liability for Huang Jianrong's obligation to pay service remuneration to Weifu Company. Second, the Consulting Intermediary Agreement was signed by Huang Jianrong in his personal name. Haicheng Company was not a party to that agreement, and Weifu Company has no sufficient evidence to prove that Huang Jianrong's act of signing the agreement with it was performed on behalf of Haicheng Company, or that Haicheng Company, apart from that agreement, reached a supplementary agreement with Weifu Company to assume the payment obligation for Huang Jianrong's debt at issue. Although Haicheng Company objectively benefited from the asset restructuring plan, according to the principle of privity of contract, Haicheng Company is not a contracting party and should not bear the contractual liability. Therefore, the original trial judgment's decision to order Haicheng Company to assume joint and several liability also lacks a basis in the parties' agreement. Finally, the original trial judgment should not have directly applied the principle of fairness and exercised its discretion to order Haicheng Company to assume joint and several liability for Huang Jianrong's obligation to pay service remuneration to Weifu Company. In civil adjudication, only when there is no specific legal provision, and in order to achieve justice in a particular case, may a court apply the basic principles and general intent of the law to adjudicate. Under normal circumstances, a court cannot directly apply the basic legal principle of "fairness principle" as a rule of adjudication; doing so would constitute an escape to a general clause and violate the basic rules of legal application. In this case, the original trial judgment used the fairness principle to hold Haicheng Company, the actual beneficiary but not a party to the contract, jointly and severally liable for Huang Jianrong's payment obligation. This lacked the autonomy of the parties' will, disregarded the parties' expectations in civil and commercial activities, and could easily lead to the abuse of discretion. In summary, absent any legal provision or contractual agreement, the original trial judgment, solely on the grounds that Huang Jianrong was the legal representative of Haicheng Company and that his engagement of Weifu Company to provide the financing services at issue was actually for the benefit of Haicheng Company, ordered Haicheng Company to assume joint and several liability for Huang Jianrong's obligation to pay service remuneration. This was indeed improper, and this court hereby corrects it.

In conclusion, the retrial claims of Huang Jianrong and Haicheng Company are partially established, and this court supports them. Pursuant to Article 214, paragraph 1, and Article 177, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2020) Hu Min Zhong No. 308 of the Shanghai High People's Court and the civil judgment (2018) Hu 02 Min Chu No. 1164 of the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court;

2. Huang Jianrong shall pay RMB 14,900,000 to Weifu International Co., Ltd. as service fee within ten days from the effective date of this judgment;

3. Dismiss the other claims of Weifu International Co., Ltd.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 186,749.36 shall be borne by Huang Jianrong in the amount of RMB 93,374.68 and by Weifu International Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 93,374.68; the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 186,749.36 shall be borne by Huang Jianrong in the amount of RMB 93,374.68 and by Weifu International Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 93,374.68.

This judgment is final.
